title: Personal Checking: Bank-Error Refunds of Overdraft Item Fees
content:
## Policy entry

Personal Checking treats an overdraft item fee that should never have been charged as the bank's error, and puts it right with a bank-error refund. The duty to do so follows from the state of the account's records and does not depend on a request from the customer. What this policy settles is whether the overdraft item fee in question comes back in full or not at all; an appeal for goodwill on a fee charged properly belongs to the courtesy refund rules instead.

## Effect on the account

A posted refund is visible in the account activity without delay, carries the label of a bank-error correction of an overdraft item fee, and raises the posted ledger balance by its amount at once.

## Invocation

The refund is booked with `refund_uncovered_overdraft_fee_6b0f4e50`, a tool from the agent's hidden set. It stays unavailable until the agent unlocks it; after that the agent calls it directly. Each call writes one refund entry, dated today, that returns one overdraft item fee entry in full as a bank-error correction. The tool accepts the amount and the fee reference exactly as given and does not itself verify the fee, its date, its amount or any refund made before.

### Parameter reference

| Name | Meaning | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `checking_account_id` | the checking account on which the overdraft item fee was charged, by its reference number from the checking account lookup | reference number |
| `customer_id` | the account owner's customer reference number from the customer profile lookup | reference number |
| `source_item_id` | the overdraft item fee entry being refunded, by its reference number in the checking activity lookup | reference number |
| `amount` | how many U.S. dollars are refunded | positive plain number to two decimals, half-up (e.g. 12.34) |
| `statement_cycle` | the statement cycle that today's posting belongs to | `YYYY-MM`, the closing month of that cycle |

### Receipt

A confirming sentence comes back naming the refund entry that was written and the overdraft item fee entry it undoes; it also reports, in USD with cents, how much was returned and what the posted ledger balance is afterwards. Getting that sentence back means the refund has posted.
